**119** They have clung to fabrications that leave one bewildered. Among other things, they have accused His Honor the Name of God, Ḥājj Sayyid Javād of Karbalā—upon him be the glory of God, the Most Glorious—of hesitating in this Cause or even, God forbid, denying it. The petitions and letters that he wrote in his own hand and sent to the Most Holy Presence are extant, some from the direction of the land of Ṭā and some from the regions of Yā and Khā, and a number of people know of them. In one letter he discussed in detail those who harbor vain imaginings, including their leader and others. God bears witness that this is stated truthfully. God has never needed, nor does He now need, these accounts. If we were to turn our attention to these matters and accounts of this kind, numerous volumes would result, each unfolding a world of its own.

**120** On one occasion these words were revealed by the Manifestation of clear proofs. His words, exalted be His glory and great be His station: “Servant in attendance! One sacrificial victim appeared in the world, and from that day until now the tongues of the people and the books in existence have spoken of him and borne witness to the loftiness of his station. We, however, sent a sacrificial victim to every place, and none returned alive from the sacrificial ground of the Friend. Each freely laid the crown of life at the feet of the Beloved of all existence with the utmost joy and longing.” End of quotation.

**121** Among them was the Beloved of Martyrs, His Honor Āqā Sayyid Ismaʿīl of Zavārih—upon him be the glory of God, the Most Glorious—who sacrificed himself by his own hand while facing the House. Although this act is outwardly reprehensible, the love of God so seized him that a flame of fire shone forth from every one of his veins. Likewise, His Honor Abā Baṣīr and Āqā Sayyid Ashraf—upon them both be the glory of God and His loving care—rose from the horizon of their home in the name of God, exalted be His glory, and openly, without concealment, spoke in praise of the Beloved of all lands. The idolaters seized them both and first sent them to prison. They summoned Ashraf’s mother to counsel her son, hoping that he might turn away from his allegiance or conceal his cause. But that steadfast, firmly grounded, and unwavering handmaid said upon entering the prison: “My son, be steadfast in the Cause of God. Never be afraid or dismayed by the might of the idolaters.” In short, he and Abā Baṣīr both gave their souls in the path of the Friend with the utmost joy and delight.

**122** And reflect on His Honor NajafʿAlī—upon him be the glory of God. As they were taking him to the sacrificial ground of the Friend, he recited this verse: “We have found both the price and the price of blood.” He repeated this verse until he attained martyrdom.

**123** Gentlemen! Hear the story of Badīʿ. Truly, in his every movement the signs of divine power and eternal majesty were plainly manifest. He arrived in the early days of the Most Great Prison, when the throne was established in the military barracks. For two days He summoned him to a private room; the door was closed, and no one else was present before Him. No one knew the purpose until He said: “God has willed a new creation,” and Badīʿ himself was unaware of it. In one passage of a Tablet this exalted utterance was revealed by the Most Exalted Pen. His words, mighty is His utterance: “We began the creation of Badīʿ, and when his creation was complete and his character refined, We sent him forth like a ball of fire,” and so on to the end of His words, exalted is He.

**124** He was then dismissed. His Honor Amīn—upon him be the glory of God—set out for his homeland, as instructed, with the Tablet to His Majesty the King. At the seaport, His Honor Badīʿ learned of the Tablet and asked to be its bearer. Everyone subsequently heard what happened. A man without weapons or equipment, wearing nothing but a cotton shirt, raised the Tablet before the king through divine strength and power and said: “I have come to you from the greatest captivity with a mighty Book,” or words to that effect. I ask for fairness: this one soul stood against the world. Yet it is no wonder that divine power should raise up a world of might within a human being. He has power over whatever He wills, and He is supreme over whatever He desires.

**125** Say: You who are without fairness! You regarded the martyrdom of the Prince of Martyrs as proof and evidence of the supreme truth of the chosen Messenger—may the souls of all others be sacrificed for Him—and likewise counted the sacrifice of Ishmael as a sign of the exalted station of both him and the Friend of God. Now reflect on these self-sacrificing souls. By the life of my Beloved and the Beloved of the world, my Desire and the Desire of the nations! His Honor Badīʿ appeared with such power and assurance that trembling and turmoil seized the pillars of authority. Surely everyone has heard, and the fair-minded do not deny it. Then, for several days, that sacred person was subjected to the severest torment and torture, yet with perfect steadfastness continued to remember and speak of the Friend. This astonished everyone, so much so that while he was in the hands of the executioners, burdened with chains and fetters, they took his photograph. Someone sent one of these to the Most Holy Presence, and it is still extant.

**126** Reflect, then, on these events, which have had no parallel or equal. This mortal does not know which sacrificial victim to recount. They arrested the father of His Honor Badīʿ—upon him be the glory of God—in the land of Khā. However much His Highness the Prince and others urged him to conceal his faith so that they could protect him from the clamor of the clergy, he refused, saying: “These are my last days, and martyrdom is more delightful and sweeter than any honey.” And he attained it.

**127** Likewise, the sacrificial victim of the land of Nūn Rā, in the land of Tā, who was named Mīrzā Muṣṭafā—upon him be the glory of God, the Most Glorious—and the souls who were with him, proceeded to the place of sacrifice with perfect steadfastness and utmost contentment, and he laid the crown of life at the feet of the Lord of names and attributes. These are souls who freely sacrificed their lives. Take heed, you who have insight!

**128** It is better now that we turn to the land of Ṣād and reflect on His Honor the King of Martyrs and the Beloved of Martyrs, and on the detachment of those two holy souls from all but God, and judge fairly. However much they were urged to conceal their faith or utter a word, they refused. With the utmost longing and eagerness, they set out for the heavenly homeland. Afterward, the Tablet of the Proof descended from the heaven of the All-Merciful’s Cause, and concerning those two souls—the Wolf and the She-Serpent—there was revealed that from which every fair-minded person perceives the fragrance of divine power and knowledge. These are His words, blessed and exalted is He: “He is the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. The winds of hatred have encompassed the Ark of Baṭḥā……” and so forth.

**129** You who possess sight, reflect a little, that you may discover the sweetness of the All-Merciful’s utterance and deliver yourselves from the desert of ignorance and unawareness. The purpose of recounting proofs, arguments, verses, and clear evidences is that closed doors may perhaps be opened and broken covenants renewed. Whatever the Most Exalted Pen revealed concerning the She-Serpent and the Wolf came to pass, and everyone witnessed it. This servant is bewildered: has understanding utterly vanished, or has fairness become as elusive as the phoenix? What has happened that the intoxication of heedlessness has encompassed everyone? What has impeded the sense of taste, and what has befallen the sense of smell? These things are nothing but the recompense for deeds. I ask God to graciously bestow His assistance.

**130** O God, O Generous One, O Merciful One! What ingratitude have Your servants shown that they have remained deprived of the waves of the ocean of mercy and barred from the radiant light of the Sun of Revelation? My God, conceal the deeds of the ignorant through Your name, the Concealer. You are the Generous One whose giving the sins of sinners have not prevented, and whose gate of grace they have not closed. One letter from the book of Your bounty became the cause of existence, and one drop from the ocean of Your mercy became the substance of the unseen and the seen. In utter helplessness, ignorance, poverty, and weakness, we seek the wonders of Your grace; we hold fast to its cord and cling to its hem. O Concealer of faults, conceal our faults and adorn us with the vesture of Your most great forgiveness. You are that Mighty One who, through a single act of will, can make the powerless the dawning places of power and the weak the sources of authority. There is no God but You, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. You are the Almighty, the All-Wise, and You are the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful, the Bountiful, the Generous.

**131** Reflect on another sacrificial victim of the land of Ṣād, His Honor Kāẓim—that sacrificial victim whose self-sacrifice illumined the horizons and whose ardor imparted warmth to creation. He offered his life in the path of the Friend in such a manner that the Concourse on high was astonished at his steadfastness, detachment, and self-sacrifice. Apart from him, a new sacrificial victim astonished the world, and the atoms of all created things have borne witness to his devotion, submission, contentment, fidelity, and steadfastness.

**132** That honored man, who lived in the land of Mīm and was known as Mullā ʿAlījān, raised the banner of divine unity in that land. He was so aflame with the heat of the love of God that he set a number of others ablaze, until the people of discord and hypocrisy broke the divine Covenant and plotted against that wronged one. Everything he possessed was plundered. Then they brought that holy being, together with a number of his associates, to the land of Ṭā in chains and fetters and sent them to ʿAlī Kandish. Through a thousand tricks and schemes, they sought to make him break God’s Covenant and efface His pledge. Yet that horseman in the arena of truth and proof had turned his eyes from all but God and had no companion, desire, or remembrance except the remembrance of the Friend, reunion with the Friend, and nearness to the Friend. In short, those who turned away and associated partners with God did not achieve their aim: no word of denial was heard from that mine of acknowledgment, until he attained his own desire and

**133** After the ascent of that sanctified spirit and the ascension of that essence of humanity, two Tablets of Visitation for him descended from the heaven of bounty and grace through the Most Exalted Pen—may the souls of all in the kingdoms of command and creation be sacrificed for Him. One of those two is recounted here, that the fragrance of justice and fairness may perhaps spread, and that people may not act on illusions and cling to conjectures as in former centuries and ages. He does whatever He wills and decrees whatever He desires, and He is the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

**134** He is the Comforter from His most exalted horizon.

**135** May the first light that appeared, shone, gleamed, and flashed from the dawn of inner meanings rest upon you, O rustling of the Tree beyond which there is no passing in the kingdom of names, and sign of Revelation in the mortal realm of creation. I bear witness, O master of the servants and light of the lands, that you were the dawning place of concord throughout the horizons, and that through your steadfastness the limbs of the people of hypocrisy trembled—those who broke the Covenant and disbelieved in God, the Lord of the Day of Meeting.

**136** Through you the banner of truth was raised among creation, His verses were manifested, His laws were spread abroad, and His clear proofs appeared. Blessed is whoever turned toward you, found companionship with you, visited your grave, perceived from you the fragrance of your Lord’s garment, circled around you, attained your presence, and spoke in remembrance of you.

**137** Through you the banner of divine unity rose above the standard in the world, and the light of eternity shone among the nations. Through your humility, necks bowed, and through your turning toward Him, faces turned toward the face of God, the Lord of lords. You were an interpreter of God’s revelation, an expounder of His verses, a bearer of His trusts, a place where His mysteries descended, a treasury for the pearls of His knowledge, a dawning place for the appearance of His lights, a source of the sweet waters of His mercy, a dayspring of His signs, and a throne on which the temple of His laws was established.

**138** I bear witness that through your arising the sincere arose, through your call the sleeping awoke, and through your turning toward Him those brought near turned toward Him and the upholders of His unity hastened. Through you the Book and the decisive utterance were manifested, and you are the one who calls out in the name of your Lord at the place of return. I bear witness that in your days the gate of reunion was opened to all in earth and heaven, and the rains of grace and bounty poured down from the cloud of generosity.

**139** Blessed are you, O joy of the chosen ones and heart of the holy ones. You are the one through whose blood God adorned the surface of the earth, and through whose body He adorned its depths. Blessed are you, O pillar of faith and dawning place of recognition. You are the one before whose remembrance all remembrances bowed, and before the appearance of whose name all names humbled themselves.

**140** Alas, alas, O most distant goal and name of God, the Lord of the throne and the earth, for what befell you at the hands of rulers and religious scholars! By God, at your affliction the very essence of joy lamented before the face of Revelation, and the dove of sorrows moaned upon the branches. Because of what befell you, the sighs of those brought near ascended and the tears of the upholders of His unity flowed.

**141** You see and know, O God of the unseen and Sovereign of the visible, that the earth is awash with the blood of Your chosen ones and Your holy ones, and that they had no mother to lament them, nor any companion to comfort their children and their wives. There befell them in the land of Ṭā that which caused the Concourse on high to lament.

**142** You have seen, O my God, Your servant ʿAlī cast upon the dust—he who was enraptured by the breezes of Your revelation, moved by Your will, and set aflame by the fire of Your love, so that everyone with hearing heard from every vein of his body the verses of Your love and the mysteries of Your guardianship. He truly strove in Your path and arose in full devotion to Your service, until he became crimson with blood before His all-knowing face and offered up his soul in longing to meet You and attain reunion with You, O Lord of eternity.

**143** At this the Maid of Glory in the highest Paradise lamented, as did the inhabitants of the loftiest heaven and the tabernacle of glory in the kingdom of names. There was no one, O my God, to carry him to his resting place, the station You had ordained for him through Your Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Scroll, and \[corrupted original text\] two of Your handmaidens who had found the sweetness of Your service in Your days and recognized what most of Your men and servants had overlooked.

**144** O Lord, bless them both in Your realm of power, then ordain for them that from which the sincere may perceive the fragrance of Your grace and loving care. O my God and God of names, my Creator and Creator of heaven, I ask You by his noble blood, by his arising for Your Cause, by his steadfastness in Your service, and by his offering up his soul in Your path, to forgive me, my parents, and whoever has believed in You and turned toward You. Then I ask You to make me firm in Your Cause, steadfast in Your love, known by Your name, and enriched by Your riches. There is no God but You, the Guardian over all that has been and all that will be.

**145** Gentlemen, speak for God's sake and listen for God's sake. Formerly, as has been stated, they cited the martyrdom of His Holiness the Lord of Martyrs—may God's peace be upon him—as the greatest proof and mightiest testimony to the Cause of His Holiness the Seal—may the souls of all others be sacrificed for Him. Yet these fervent, assured souls, content with God and pleasing to Him, who soared on the wings of detachment to the realm of sacrifice and freely gave their lives in the path of the Beloved of all existence, have escaped the notice of the heedless and those who associate partners with God. Their desires have veiled them, and their delusions have enveloped them. By the life of God, the martyrdom of each of these souls is a greater proof and a more perfect and complete demonstration. Yet God, exalted be His glory, has spoken of nothing in proof of His blessed Cause except what has been sent down from Him and has appeared from His presence.

**146** O people of understanding, reflect on what flowed from the pen of the Primal Point—may the souls of all others be sacrificed for Him—in the eighth chapter of the sixth Váḥid. His words, exalted be He: “It has been commanded that once every nineteen days they consider this chapter, so that, at the appearance of Him Whom God will make manifest, they may not be veiled by matters other than the verses, which have been and remain the greatest of proofs and demonstrations.”

**147** In this chapter He says—His words, blessed and exalted be He: “After the setting of the Sun of Truth, it is impossible for a verse to appear from anyone other than Him, through innate capacity and power, without learning or the means that people of learning can conceive. Although it is impossible for anyone other than Him Whom God will make manifest to claim this, it has been enjoined in the Bayán that if anyone makes such a claim and verses appear from him, no one should oppose him, lest any sorrow befall that Sun of Truth.” And further, in His words, mighty and glorious is He:

**148** “If you hear of such a claim and are not convinced, do nothing that would cause him sorrow, even if in reality he is someone other than Him. Although this is an impossible supposition, the mere fact that he has mentioned His name makes it unworthy of those who love Him to cause him sorrow, out of respect for His name. For the matter admits of only two possibilities: either it is He—and it is impossible for anyone other than Him to reveal verses through innate capacity—so why should anyone deny the Truth when night and day he has acted in expectation of Him? Or, supposing the impossible, someone has attributed himself to Him; then let them leave his judgment to God. It is not for people to judge him, out of reverence for the name of their Beloved. Yet there is no such soul who can claim such a station. If such a person appeared in the cycle of the Qurʼán, one will appear in this cycle as well.

**149** “His verses are in themselves proof of the radiance of the sun of His being, and the powerlessness of all is proof of their poverty and need for Him. The reason for this command is that, on the day of the appearance of the Truth, their feet may not slip on the path, nor may they, because of a phantom in their hearts, use that verse to pass a judgment against the Creator of their own existence that would at once nullify their entire being and all their deeds without their even knowing it.

**150** “If all obey this one command, it is for God to make the Truth manifest to them and to instill proof and evidence in their hearts through the manifest proofs that shine forth from Him, so that they may express certainty concerning Him, and concerning others may express suspension of judgment, for suspension of judgment applies to those other than the Truth. If all the people of the Bayán act according to this command, it will suffice for their salvation on the Day of Resurrection. For that is the day when all on earth, through what shines in their hearts from the Sun of Truth, will say, ‘We act for God.’ But the truthful are those servants who look, through God, mighty and glorious is He, to the Creator of the verses, who is that Sun of Truth whose verses, which are His radiance, distinguish between all things. Such is God's proof, now made complete for you. O servants of God, then fear Me.”

**151** O people of insight, consider this utterance of the All-Merciful, whose fragrance has encompassed the world and whose intent is manifest, evident, and clear. This chapter is indeed a strong shield and sturdy armor for the protection of the Desire of all peoples. O people of the Bayán, have some shame and reflect a little. His verses have encompassed the world; every atom of creation has testified and continues to testify to His greatness. Fear God, exalted be His glory, and do not set aside the provisions and utterances of His Holiness the Herald for selfish aims.

**152** The Desired One—may the souls of all in the kingdoms of command and creation be sacrificed for Him—has relinquished your assistance, acknowledgment, and faith. I say this in truth, for it has been heard from His blessed lips: “Turn to whatever door you wish, drink from whatever cup you desire, and go in whatever direction and toward whatever place you choose. But leave this Wronged One to Himself, with these resplendent verses and clear proofs, standing against His enemies. Abandon your stratagems, scheming, deceit, and deception.”

**153** This mortal submits: Pursue your own intentions with complete assurance; He will never interfere, even if at every moment you take for yourselves a lord other than God. But do not commit an act that would burn the heart of the Primal Point and make the eyes of grandeur weep. Let them read one of the revealed surahs alongside the Bayán and all the divine scriptures, so that what you have overlooked may become clear to you. Know with evident certainty and testify to that to which the Point of the Bayán—may the souls of all in existence be sacrificed for Him—has testified. He says: “The whole of the Bayán does not equal a single one of His verses.” This is the truth, beyond all doubt.

**154** As for the person to whom you now cling—by the life of my Desired One and the Desired One of all in earth and heaven—you have never been, and are not now, aware of his affair, and this servant too is forbidden to speak of it. Perhaps its time will come. If only the sun of permission would shine from the highest horizon, and this servant could relate what he knows. The pen is bewildered, the ink is bewildered, the world is bewildered. What has happened? They are engrossed in the buzzing of a fly and turn away from the Lord of Lords. They have broken God's covenant and turned their eyes away from His pledge.

**155** If anyone reflects on the humility and submissiveness of the Point of the Bayán before the manifestation of this Name, he will testify to what has flowed from the Most Exalted Pen. By the Sun of Truth, so great were His humility and submissiveness that the Most Exalted Pen is powerless to describe them.

**156** How fitting it is to mention here this passage, which has just come to this mortal's mind. In the days when the son of Zechariah appeared and was engaged in baptism, traveling in the wilderness and proclaiming the glad tidings, he said: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.” He says: “Repent and turn back to God, for the divine kingdom has drawn near.” “I baptize you with water for repentance, but He who comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to carry.” He gave the people glad tidings of the appearance of His Holiness the Spirit, saying: “He is mightier, and I am not worthy to carry His shoes.”

**157** Although His Holiness the Spirit and he lived in the same day, because the Cause of His Holiness the Spirit was concealed at that time, he says, “And He who comes after me,” meaning, “He will manifest Himself after me.” Then he says: “Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him. But John prevented Him, saying, ‘I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?’ Jesus answered and said to him, ‘Listen now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all \[corrupted original text\].’”

**158** Yasúʿ is His Holiness Christ, and John is the son of Zechariah. In the books he is called John the Baptist, for baptism is among his ordinances; it is now practiced and upheld among Christians, and they observe it. In short, the fragrance of these days was wafting in those days, just as His Holiness the Point—may the souls of all others be sacrificed for Him—filled the entire Bayán with the glad tidings of this Revelation. By the life of God, if anyone inhales with justice and fairness the fragrance of the words of the Bayán, one by one, he will find in them nothing but the fragrance of love for this Revelation. Every fair-minded and just person bears witness to this, but most of the people are among those who deny.

**159** O people of the Bayán, listen to what this servant submits, and enter the path with complete assurance, placing your trust in God. Caution today is counted among the greatest sins and has been and will remain in the fire. The pen of the Primal Point has testified to this. His words, blessed and exalted be He: “Recognize Him by His verses and exercise no caution in recognizing Him, for to that same extent you will remain veiled in the fire.” End of quotation.

**160** Break the idols, tear apart the veils of conjecture, and look to the Most Exalted Horizon alone, so that you may attain true recognition of divine unity on the Day of God. I swear by the sun of the horizon of the heaven of grace: each thing manifested in this Most Great Revelation is like the sun at its zenith. None denies them except those who are heedless and beset by doubt. Hear these words for the sake of God and act upon them. The proof and testimony by which you acknowledged the Point of the Bayán and the Messengers of the past now exist in a greater and more perfect form. Consider this, and speak with justice and fairness.

**161** I ask God’s forgiveness for my mention, my exposition, and my speech. The world is not devoid of people of fairness, justice, and knowledge. Those possessed of knowledge should certainly examine what has been sent down in Arabic and Persian from the Most Exalted Pen in this Revelation, as well as what was previously sent down to the Prophets and Messengers, and speak with fairness and express themselves with justice.

**162** I ask Your forgiveness, O God of existence, for any mention from which those brought near to You perceive the scent of comparison and limitation. O Lord, purify the sight of Your creatures from everything that prevents them from looking to You and placing their trust in You. O Lord, adorn them with the vesture of justice and fairness, and illumine their hearts with the lights of Your knowledge. You are indeed powerful over all things.

**163** On one occasion, the Dawning-place of the Verses and Manifestation of Clear Proofs said: “O servant in attendance, know with manifest certainty that God—exalted be His glory—has an established right, a manifest Cause, and a resplendent light. He renders all the objections of the people of the Bayán nonexistent, null, and void through a single utterance He previously spoke.” His words—exalted be His utterance: “He does whatever He wills and decrees whatever He desires.”

**164** If a soul truly holds fast to this exalted utterance and is certain of it, that soul will turn to none but Him, see none but Him, accept nothing from anyone but Him, and say with both the outward and the inward tongue:

**165** “O my God and my heart’s desire, praise be to You for revealing Yourself, sending down Your verses, bringing forth Your clear proofs, and sending that from which everyone endowed with a sense of smell has perceived the fragrance of Your garment, the sweet scents of Your days, and the perfumes of Your Revelation.

**166** O Lord, strengthen my heart so that the allusions of those among Your creatures who turn away, and of the faithless among Your servants, may not prevent it from turning toward Your horizon. Strengthen my hand, O my God, to take hold of Your Book with a certainty that makes the hearts of those among Your creatures who associate partners with You tremble. Illumine my face with the lights of Your face, and adorn my being with the vesture of steadfastness in Your love.

**167** O Lord, this is Your Day. I testify that in it, through Your Revelation, mysteries have been disclosed, trees have borne fruit, the rule of divine unity has been established, all forms of limitation have been effaced, the banner of utterance has been raised upon the highest spot in the contingent world, and Your call has risen at all times.

**168** O Lord, I ask You by Your name the All-Bountiful, by Your name the Preserver, and by Your name the Helper, not to leave me to myself. Rescue me with the arms of Your power, and then protect me from those people of the Bayán who have broken Your covenant, shattered Your pledge, cast aside Your laws, disputed Your verses, and rejected Your proof when You came to them from the heaven of certitude with the banners of wisdom and utterance. You are indeed powerful to do whatever You will, and in Your grasp are the reins of all things. There is no God but You, the Strong, the Almighty.” End of quotation.

**169** Glory be to God! What has happened that people have barred and deprived themselves of God, manifest, resplendent, and plainly visible, and cling to and occupy themselves with the words of this person and that? Such things have never been new, nor are they now. Throughout the centuries and ages, they have clung to the cords of delusion, and after the Sun of Truth has appeared and the fabrications have been exposed, they have failed to awaken and have returned to their starting point without realizing it. It is as though they deserve to be afflicted once again by the preaching of preachers and the snares of the ignorant.

**170** Gentlemen, reflect on the events of the past and their fruits and consequences, so that you may remain protected from the likes of those rebellious, defiant souls. Truly, the fruits of their deeds are a great admonition, a mighty counsel, and a profound lesson.

**171** What, then, can this servant say? By the life of our Beloved and the Beloved of all who are in earth and heaven, delusions are seen among some of the people of the Bayán the like of which have never appeared before. In one of the cities, a knowledgeable member of the people of God conversed with one of these deluded people, reciting the revealed verses of the Bayán and citing them as evidence for his point. The deluded man denied it, saying, “What you say is not in the Bayán.” The other then brought the Bayán and showed him the passage written by His Holiness. The man said, “This Bayán is not authentic.” He replied, “Go and bring the Bayán that you have.” He said, “That is not authentic either.” He asked, “Where, then, is the authentic Bayán?” He answered, “With His Holiness.”

**172** The foul odor of this statement carries the odor of words spoken in the past, as when they used to say, “Ten sections of the Qur’an have been stolen, and the complete Qur’an is with the Qá’im, who will bring it.” O God, O God! “They have made the Qur’an into fragments,” meaning that they divided it, that is, tore it into pieces: a thief carried off some of it, and they altered some of it.

**173** This evanescent servant testifies that the Qur’an was complete and that the Bayán is also complete. The Qur’an is the very one that has been in everyone’s hands, and the Bayán is likewise the very one that now exists. But that liar’s purpose is to close the roads and bar the paths, to make whatever arises from conjecture an authority, and to afflict the people, just as others have done before.

**174** In any case, the hope is that the Hand of Power will ward off these new veils and awaken the hapless people. Those people are shameless. The words of that heedless man give rise to delusions. Glory be to God! What has happened to the people of the Bayán that they consider the truthful a liar and the liar truthful, like the lost sect that regarded itself as saved? For twelve hundred years—indeed, longer—they have called and continue to call Ja‘far a liar, although that wronged man spoke a single statement in accordance with truth, honesty, and sincerity.

**175** There are now many heedless, deluded souls who turn away. Among them is Mírzá Hádí Dawlatábádí, who considers himself the people’s guide and leader. I swear by God Himself that, by night and day, he was occupied with transcribing the verses revealed in His presence, while the concealed person was unable to speak in His presence. These hapless people do not know. They have listened out of desire, cling to desire, and hold fast to desire. In the end, the fruits of their deeds and words, like those of the people of the Qur’an, have been and will be scattered dust.

**176** I ask God to bestow fairness and remove the old rancor and hatred from among His creatures. Yet this is very difficult, for how can souls nurtured in conjectures and delusions throughout the centuries and ages be worthy to behold the lights of the Sun of Certitude?

**177** This servant is forbidden to disclose and mention certain matters; otherwise, things would be said of which the servants have until now remained heedless and unaware. His words—exalted be His glory and all-embracing His bounty: “O servant in attendance, We speak within measure, not as befits the kingdom of My utterance and the dominion of My knowledge, unless We see the House empty of all but Me.” End of quotation.

**178** By God, this servant has spoken and will speak for the sake of God, and has had and has no ulterior aim. My Lord, the All-Merciful, is indeed independent of the faith of those people of the Bayán who have broken His covenant and made war against Him.

**179** The Point of the Bayán—may the souls of all others be sacrificed for Him—says that on that Day the Sun of Truth will address the people of the Bayán and recite this surah of the Qur’an. His words, exalted be He: “Say: O unbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. To you your religion, and to me mine.”

**180** In these days this blessed surah has repeatedly been heard from the Tongue of Eternity. Blessed are the fair-minded, blessed are the discerning, and blessed are those who reflect. It is incumbent on every soul today, through the power and might of God—exalted be His glory—to protect the horizon of the Sun of Certitude from the clouds of conjecture and delusion, although He Himself has ever been and remains the Protector of all. The purpose of what is said in these passages is that His servants may attain the privilege of serving His Cause. The world’s one or two hours have never been and are not worthy of mention. The hope is that He will not close the door of grace or deprive His loved ones of His fragrance.

**181** Gentlemen! An entire chapter of the Bayán is devoted specifically to this statement. He says: “The tree of affirmation, by turning away from Him, is reckoned among those of negation, and the tree of negation, by turning toward Him, is reckoned among those of affirmation.” In short, tell those caught in delusion: today is a mighty day, illumined by the light of divine unity. There has never been, nor is there now, any scope for defining partners with God, as they spent years doing. Supreme infallibility has always belonged, and still belongs, exclusively to the sanctified Essence; no one else has any share in it. And He proclaims at the heart of creation: “There is no God but Him, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.”

**182** People of the Bayán! Listen to the words of this transitory servant, and do not rise up in oppression as did the people of the Qur’an. All the divines of that community practiced the utmost oppression, yet considered themselves oppressed. Fear God, people, and do not be among the oppressors. Although He says that if a soul makes a claim without producing any proof, you must not interfere with him or cause him sorrow, now, despite proofs and testimonies that have encompassed the world and whose light has illumined the outer world and the world within, they have said what no oppressor, earlier or later, has ever said.

**183** For God’s sake, reflect, that you may find the pearls of utterance in the ocean of meanings. All His utterances were a mercy for His servants. Do not make them a scourge for yourselves and those who come after you. Roll up the arrangements of past and future, and enter with the utmost joy and delight into this gathering now spread before you. I ask God—exalted be His glory—to assist those who turn away and deny in returning, repenting, and turning humbly to Him. What a great pity it would be to make yourselves deserving of scourges and unending wrath.

**184** Can this blessed, exalted Tree, whose branch rises higher than a hundred thousand heavens, be denied? Is there any room left for hesitation or debate? No, by His own Self, the True One! Unless divine wrath should seize someone in requital for their deeds. Glory be to God! Heedless souls have sought to conceal the Sun of Truth. This couplet is fitting here:

**185** "These clods of clay intend, out of envy, to conceal Your sun."

**186** Such calamities have befallen the blessed Tree that anyone who reflected on them even briefly would take their own life. Since this has been forbidden, this servant and others like him have remained alive. I swear by the Sun of the horizon of truthfulness: the pens of the world are powerless to recount them, and the hearts of the Concourse on high are burning.

**187** Among these afflictions was this: in this land, after the arrival in the Most Great Prison, two heedless, veiled souls associated with everyone and, in every gathering, gave each person an account. God knows what befell Him through them in the regions and lands of exile. They mixed some of the surahs with their own fabrications and gave a sheet to everyone—by God, besides whom there is no other God, even to the town’s scavenger. Matters reached the point where the fire of sedition was kindled and the blaze of hatred flared up from hearts and souls. At last, the Lord of all issued an order that the door be closed. For several months He met with no one, whether from within or without. The door was closed, and seekers were barred and kept away.

**188** Then, one night, while this transitory one was in His presence, occupied in transcribing the verses, the blessed tone suddenly changed. These exalted, mighty, triumphant, all-subduing verses were revealed in such a manner that this servant’s limbs trembled. God is my witness and testimony that no assurance or tranquility whatsoever remained in my soul. His words—exalted be His glory, all-embracing His bounty, and mighty His utterance: “The ocean of tribulation has surged, and the waves have encompassed the Ark of God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.” On hearing this blessed verse, no life remained in this servant. Then this verse was revealed: “O Mariner, do not be troubled by the winds, for the Cleaver of the Dawn is with Us in this darkness that has encompassed the worlds.” From this verse some tranquility was gained, but it became clear and certain that a dark upheaval lay ahead.

**189** In short, everything that happened afterward was revealed, word for word, in that blessed Tablet. Among other things, He says: “At times We render assistance through the hands of rulers, ambassadors, and loved ones, and at times through the hands of enemies.” The following afternoon, this servant was in His presence, occupied in transcribing the verses, when an uproar arose. All the townspeople and the soldiery appeared before the house with drawn swords. The shameful deeds of those souls took tangible form, and what happened, happened. For a time this servant was anxious and trembling, lest any sorrow befall the Ancient Beauty. By the life of our Lord, had it been left to God, He Himself would have sufficed, just as He sufficed against the Wolf, the She-Serpent, and others like them.

**190** Afterward, the sister of Riḍā-Qulī took a bundle of revealed surahs and Tablets, including the Surah of the Chief, and handed it to the governor of the town, supposing that he would rise up in opposition. Instead, the decree of the revealed verse became manifest. The governor read some of them, rose in the morning, and went to His Holiness the Most Great Branch of God—may my soul and my being be sacrificed at His feet—bringing all the surahs and handing them over. He said: “Last night I examined these Tablets, and the greatness of the Cause seized me. I knew with certainty that this Cause is true, for if we deny Him, we must deny all the Messengers and Scriptures.” And he requested an audience and admission to His presence.

**191** Eventually, one day, a man named ʿAbbūd, who owned the house, came before Him and asked that His Excellency the governor be admitted to His presence. He consented, and after entering His presence, the governor attained faith and certitude and carried out everything he was commanded to do. Great relief came to all the prisoners who were in this city.

**192** The point is that they carried out everything within the power of heedless souls. They so misled all the people of this land that whenever they saw any of these captives, they uttered offensive words. In short, they caused the door of mercy to be closed to everyone for several months. God knows what befell Him at the hands of His enemies. Anyone possessing even an atom of justice and fairness will testify that no Revelation more exalted, more glorious, or more manifest than this Revelation has appeared in the world.

**193** Have those who turn away not heard the account of the challenge to invoke God’s judgment that took place in the Land of Mystery? By the life of our Desired One, what came to pass astonished the people of the city. Since some may not have heard of it, a brief account is therefore given, so that the fair-minded may be informed and perhaps those who turn away may also find the way.

**194** After the arrival in the Land of Mystery, one day Siyyid Muḥammad-i-Iṣfahānī came into His presence and presented a matter, which was not accepted. A few days earlier, too, the Tongue of Grandeur had addressed him in these words: “Muḥammad, you have no knowledge or awareness of the ways of the Prophets and the character of the chosen ones.” End of quotation. \[corrupted original text\]

**195** From this blessed utterance it appeared that he had repeated to certain people some of the sayings of the mystics of old. A few days later he again requested permission to enter. Having entered His presence, he said: “I ask that You instruct Mīrzā Yaḥyā not to write anything, for Āqā Muḥammad-ʿAlī-i-Iṣfahānī asked him about a Persian verse, and he failed to understand its meaning.” The Ancient Beauty said: “Siyyid, what business do you have with such meddling?” At last He dismissed him.

**196** He then went and misled Mīrzā Yaḥyā, outwardly professing faith in him before certain people, although—by the Self of the True One, may the souls of all in the kingdoms of revelation and creation be sacrificed for Him—during the journey the two repeatedly argued over certain matters. This finally led to confrontation, and both came into His presence and began complaining about one another. This transitory servant has no wish to give a detailed account of those souls.

**197** Brothers! By God, besides whom there is no other God, I speak truthfully: I have no purpose except that thick veils of illusion and false splendors should not once again obstruct and deprive these helpless servants. The person mentioned associated with seventy people day and night during this journey; nevertheless, he wrote to various places: “I associated with no one,” and those caught in delusion accepted it. Such is the condition of the people. I ask God to strengthen His loved ones, so that the doors of falsehood may not be opened as before, nor imaginary cities and lands be built up.

**198** After the Most Great Separation, the aforementioned Sayyid arose at the instigation of several Persians outside the community who were in that city, and associated with them day and night. Eventually, in their presence, he stated, “We have agreed to a mutual invocation of God’s judgment.” He mentioned this because he was confident that the Ancient Beauty would pay no attention to such people and would certainly not join them in a gathering. Thus, with complete assurance, he occupied himself among the Persians with these fanciful statements.

**199** Meanwhile, a man named Mīr Muḥammad arrived. He had attained the presence of the Primal Point—may the souls of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—in the Land of Shīn, and had also accompanied Him on the journey to the Great City. He learned of the Sayyid’s statements among the Persians and said, “Set the time. I will go and ask in the Most Holy Court that He come, so that truth may be clearly and conclusively distinguished from falsehood.” It was agreed that this should take place in the Mosque of Sulṭān Salīm.

**200** The aforementioned Mīr arrived and related the details to some of the friends, until the matter was submitted in His presence. This transitory servant was not present at that moment. As soon as He heard it, the Ancient Beauty rose from His seat and, alone and unaccompanied, set out toward the appointed place. Along the way, the Euphrates of divine verses flowed and descended in such a manner that no one could describe it.

**201** At that moment this servant was in the market attending to some household affairs. After hearing the news, I set out with all speed. Along the way, I saw a group of townspeople standing in astonishment on both sides of the road.

**202** When they saw this servant, they gestured with their hands to indicate, “He went this way.” When this servant entered the congregational mosque, he saw the ocean of verses surging. By the life of Him who is my Desire and the Desire of all in the heavens and on earth! The verses were descending in such a manner that everyone was bewildered, wondering what had happened. One of the Persians was seen trembling and weeping. None of the companions was in His presence except Mīr Muḥammad and this servant, who arrived afterward, for He had forbidden them all to attend.

**203** Then He turned His blessed face toward Mīr Muḥammad and said, “Muḥammad, go to them and say, ‘Come with your ropes and your rods.’” Mīr went with all speed. On returning, he reported, “The gentlemen have regretted what they said and have offered the excuse that today is not possible.” He said, “Tell them they have three days’ grace. Whichever day you present yourselves, We are ready.” He then spent a while in prayer in the mosque—a wondrous prayer. After returning, as soon as He entered the house, a Tablet was revealed in His own blessed handwriting and sealed with His blessed seal, stating, “Come on any day within three days; We are ready.” He sent that Tablet to the companions so that all would be informed. Mīr also went and conveyed the details of the Tablet, but no sign of those people appeared.

**204** Gentlemen, reflect on how manifest the Cause is and how heedless the people are. Apart from the inhabitants of that city, nearly a hundred emigrants and travelers were gathered there, and all bear witness and testify to this matter. That blessed Tablet still exists. The Sūrih of the Mutual Invocation was revealed, detailing that day, and was sent, as instructed, to one of the faithful to read to the loved ones and friends of God. Surely most have had the privilege of hearing it. A portion of it is recorded here, so that the world of existence may be illumined by the verses of the All-Merciful and the hearts of the world adorned with justice and fairness. Authority rests in God’s hand. This is what has descended from the dominion of the will of our Lord, the Almighty, the All-Knowing. His words—exalted be His glory—are: “Indeed,

**205** O Most Exalted Pen, recount to your namesake the news of this city, that he may be informed. When Muḥammad came to you from those who associate partners with God and said, ‘They wish to meet with You in another place,’ We left the house with manifest authority as soon as We heard.

**206** And We said, ‘Muḥammad, the Spirit has left His dwelling, and with Him have come forth the souls of the chosen ones and the realities of the Messengers. Look, that you may see the Concourse on High above My head, while in My grasp are the proofs of the Prophets. Open your eyes: this is ʿAlī, and then Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, who has appeared above the horizon of the house with manifest authority. Say: He has come with the banners of the verses from God, the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.’

**207** Say: Were all the learned and the mystics on earth, and then the kings and sovereigns, to gather together, I would appear before them, proclaiming the verses of God, the King, the Almighty, the All-Wise. I am He who fears no one, even if all in the heavens and the earths should unite to harm Me. The verses have bowed before My face, and voices have been hushed before My mighty, wondrous call.

**208** Say: This is My hand, which God has made white for all to behold, and it is My rod: were We to cast it down, it would swallow the earth and all who are upon it. I am the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

**209** Muḥammad, go to those who associate partners with God with the messages of God, the Lord of the worlds. Say: The Youth has come to you, and with Him are the hosts of revelation and inspiration. The Kingdom walks before Him, and behind Him are the tribes of the Concourse on High, the inhabitants of the cities of names, and the angels who are brought near.

**210** Say: Fear God, and do not oppose Him by whose command every wise decree has been ordained. Say: Come with your ropes, your rods, and whatever you possess, if you are able. We are going to the house of God which one of the kings built and which is called Salīm, and I shall remain there until the sun sets in its place of setting, so that God’s proof and demonstration may be made complete for them and they may be among those who repent.

**211** Say: Today every bond of affiliation has been severed, except for those who have entered beneath the shadow of this radiant, luminous Cause. Whoever clings to any name while turning away from the One who brought the names into being is not of Me, and God disavows him. We created the names just as We created all things, if you are among those who understand.

**212** Say: I have manifested Myself for God, and I have come forth for God. I speak before all who are on earth just as I speak before you. Truly, I fear no one. My actions bear witness to this, if you are among those who understand.

**213** Say: The signs of the True One are as manifest as the sun’s radiance and light. By God, they are even more manifest to everyone with keen sight. Do you imagine that anyone besides Him can stand alongside Him? No, by His own exalted and mighty Self! Those who have devoted themselves to names are worshippers of idols, if you are among those who see.

**214** The Prophet is the one who has informed the people of this most upright, most ancient, eternal Announcement. The Messenger is the one who has conveyed My messages and guided those who have lost the way. The Imam is the one who has stood before My face in manifest humility. The guardian is the one who has taken refuge in the firm and mighty stronghold of My guardianship. The appointed successor is the one who has enjoined upon the people what has come to him in a preserved Tablet.

**215** The one whom those who associate partners with God have taken as a lord for themselves, and on whose account they have turned against God, the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the All-Beautiful, was but one of the servants, and used to appear before the Face every morning and evening. The winds of desire blew upon him from his own self, because one of the devils led him astray. We made his name renowned among the servants through a wisdom of Our own. Your Lord is indeed the One who decrees whatever He wills.” End of quotation.

**216** Friends, a single truthful reminder suffices for one possessed of sight and understanding. At this moment I attained His presence, and the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these words—exalted be His utterance: “Servant who is present, say: You who are unfair! Have you not beheld the waves of the ocean of utterance, or have you not seen the radiance of the lights of the sun of Revelation? Fear God. Turn from the pool to the ocean, and from illusion to certainty. Today all His Books depend upon and are subject to ‘No’ and ‘Yes.’ This is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, if you understand. This Revelation has been and remains wondrous in every respect. Blessed are those who recognize it.”

**217** “Say: Would that My thoughts were your thoughts! I do not walk in your ways. I have made My path clear, manifested My proof, sent down My verses, and summoned the servants to My horizon. Some have turned toward Me, and others have turned away. Whoever has turned toward Me is indeed numbered among those who have attained success in a clear Book.” End of quotation.

**218** Would that those who turn away would look with the eye of justice at a single page of the Book of Certitude and judge fairly. Nothing previously revealed in this manner equals it. Today all are seen on a single plane. Whoever has held fast to the firm cord and clung to the luminous hem is inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Scroll as one of the people of Bahā. Today every atom bears witness and testifies to the greatness of the Cause, while those who turn away remain heedless and astray.

**219** The Most Exalted One—may the spirit of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—appealed, at the end of His commentaries, to the testimony of two scholars as proof of His truth: Mullā ʿAbd al-Khāliq and Ḥājj Mullā Muḥammad ʿAlī Barqānī Qazvīnī. He says—exalted and mighty are His words: “And \[corrupted original text\] suffices as a witness concerning Me in this matter.” End of quotation.

**220** Yet, after reading the blessed Tablet in which He says, “I am indeed the Qāʾim whose appearance you have been promised,” the first person turned away, and did so vehemently; the second likewise did not turn toward Him thereafter, nor did he seek proximity to anyone, for these two had submitted their petitions at the beginning of the Cause. Now consider how many scholars, mystics, and jurists have been seen humble and submissive before the radiance of the Sun of this Most Great Revelation. If their names were mentioned, there would, outwardly, be reason to fear harm to them.

**221** Every fair-minded person bears witness. A learned and knowledgeable person is bewildered by the actions of those who turn away and the words of the deniers. At times they speak of the Mirror, and at others of the appointed successor. These days, people in Kirmān have contrived divinity for their own leader, while another person, from Kāẓimayn and residing in Kirmānshāh, has recounted the parable of the Byzantine and the Chinese. By God, they and all they possess are like spiders’ webs—indeed, frailer still, if only they would judge fairly.

**222** Say: You hapless people, where have you been? Has anyone other than the True One Himself been manifest? Has any power been witnessed from anyone besides Him? How astonishing that people who have had no knowledge of the beginning of the Cause should issue rulings!

**223** O Muḥammad, by the life of God, you are heedless and unaware. This servant has not seen you, but for the sake of God he says: Fear God. Return to the True One. While the door is open, do not deprive yourself. Those who have prompted you were themselves unaware and had gained no share of the ocean of knowledge. The writings of the person you have taken as a lord besides God are in your possession; you have seen and read them. Now read one page of the verses of the True One and judge fairly for yourself.

**224** The Primal Point—may the spirit of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—says, exalted and mighty are His words: “Even if all the people of the Bayān should become like him in the essence of knowledge, it bears no fruit except through acknowledgment of Him. Take heed, then, O possessors of knowledge, and fear Him.” End of quotation.

**225** O my brother, anyone who denies this Cause and remains heedless of this Most Great Revelation has never been, and is not now, capable of proving any cause. Sorrow has surrounded this mortal one on every side to such a degree that he is powerless to express it, for he is adducing evidence for the Sun of Truth after its appearance and radiance, and this is a grave error. He proclaims in the loudest voice: “I am sanctified above all that has been mentioned and written. My proof is what has appeared from Me, and My testimony is My own Self, if you are among those who understand.” End of quotation.

**226** But since this servant has seen that some are weak, he has clung to the cord of reasoning, so that perhaps they may drink the everlasting Kawthar from the wellspring of divine words and attain eternal life. Otherwise, evidence itself is ashamed to be attributed to Him, and proof blushes to bow down before Him. How well it has been said:

**227** The True One has appeared, plain as the radiant sun; alas that He has come into a city of the blind.

**228** It befits a human being to be adorned with justice and fairness. The Lord of existence has Himself arisen before the world, has unsealed the choice wine through His name, the Self-Subsisting, and from His blessed Pen has flowed and descended the equivalent of all that has been sent down before and after. How can anyone hesitate in this station, or, God forbid, utter an unworthy word? The Primal Point pressed the Bayān in the hand of power; its pure essence is this blessed utterance: “He is not to be consulted on the basis of My indication.”

**229** One day the Desire of the worlds spoke these exalted words—glorified be His glory: “O servant who is present, today, if the Point Himself should hesitate in this Cause, He would be deprived of the word of approval. The people are in the sleep of heedlessness, while the eye of God watches and witnesses from the Most Exalted Horizon.” End of quotation.

**230** Anyone with a sense of smell perceives the fragrance of the All-Merciful’s utterance. The True One is as manifest and evident as His own existence. He has torn through the veils and rent the coverings of glory. Do not become a cause of these again, and do not, as before, leave the hapless people afflicted in the wilderness of vain imaginings. Fear God, O people of the Bayān, and do not be among the unjust.

**231** The Primal Point—may the spirit of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—was occupied, from the beginning of His revelation to its end, with the mention of this blessed Name. He never ceased to encourage the people of the Bayān. Every blessed expression and every holy and goodly word revealed in the Bayān He ascribed to the True One, glorified be His glory.

**232** Glory be to God! Ignorance and folly have reached such a degree, and malice and hatred such an intensity, that they have prevented ears from listening. I swear by the Sun of the horizon of meanings: if some of the verses revealed concerning this Most Great Revelation were cast upon a stone, rivers would surely gush from it.

**233** On one occasion these exalted words were heard from the tongue of the Lord of all people: “O servant who is present, the utterances that have appeared in this Revelation from the kingdom of divine knowledge bestow ears and impart their message. Do not be saddened by what this person or that person says. If a single soul discovers the sweetness of the All-Merciful’s utterance, that soul is, in God’s sight, above all who are on earth in precedence, excellence, manifestness, knowledge, and loftiness.” End of quotation.

**234** The Primal Point—may the spirit of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—says: “If on the day of His appearance there is a single believing soul, the resurrection of all the Prophets takes place in that soul.” Whenever this servant considers the power, grandeur, and sovereignty of the True One, glorified be His glory, the doors of hope open. He therefore entreats Him not to deprive anyone on earth of the breezes of His days. But when the heedlessness of the people of the Bayān and the rancor and hatred of those souls are considered, utter despair ensues.

**235** Although this servant, as he sees it, has sought through these writings to awaken souls and make them aware, it is evident that the Primal Point—may the spirit of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—has spoken of this Most Great Revelation in such a manner that nothing beyond it can be conceived. Nevertheless, He says: “They will not be willing to accord Him even the name of believer, for if they were willing, they would not bring sorrow upon Him.”

**236** In truth, this utterance of the Point of the Bayān—may the spirit of all in the contingent world be sacrificed for Him—is a book of admonition, a volume of counsel, and a scroll of awakening. Yet it only increases the loss of the unjust, the denial of the heedless, and the flight of the transgressors.

**237** This mortal one submits before everyone, his heart free of suspicions and vain imaginings and of rancor and hatred toward any soul: If the Point of the Bayān, that is, its Revealer, were to say, “O people of the Bayān, on what evidence and proof have you remained veiled from this Most Great Revelation?”, what answer would you seize upon and cling to?

**238** If you say that you have become veiled because of Me, every atom of creation bears witness and testifies that I took the covenant of allegiance to Him before taking the covenant of allegiance to Myself. “Glory be to You, O God! Bear witness that through that Book I have taken from all things the covenant of allegiance to Him whom You will make manifest before the covenant of allegiance to Myself. You and those who have believed in Your verses suffice as witnesses concerning Me. You are indeed sufficient for Me. In You have I placed My trust, and You have ever taken account of all things.”

**239** And in words more evident than the sun in the midst of heaven, I counseled everyone not to remain veiled by Me from that Desire of the worlds. The Book itself bears witness and testifies. And if, because of the Bayān, you have remained deprived of that Sovereign of days, every line and every leaf of it bears witness and testifies that I proclaimed in the loudest voice: Do not let the whole Bayān, or its Revealer, its Manifestation, and its Sovereign, deprive you of Him.

**240** If you are looking to an attribute and have been kept from the Possessor of all attributes, I have stated with complete explicitness that everything spoken of favorably in the Bayān was intended to refer to that Sun of Revelation. And if the word “mirror” has veiled you from the Sun of Meanings, this has been revealed in the Book: “O suns of the mirrors! You look toward the Sun of Truth, for your existence depends on it, if only you could perceive. You are all like fish moving through the water in the sea, yet you are veiled from the water and ask about that upon which your existence depends.” And so on, to My words: “I will surely complain to You, O Mirror of My bounty, of all the mirrors: each looks toward Me in its own colors.”

**241** And if mention of the fruit has left you veiled: “This is My covenant and My pledge with My Lord, before and after. Make that Tree, O God, entirely His, so that from it may appear the fruits of what God has created within it for Him through whom God has willed to manifest whatever He has willed. By Your might, I have never desired that there should be upon that Tree any branch, leaf, or fruit that will not bow down before Him on the day of His appearance, or will not glorify You through Him as befits the loftiest heights of His manifestation and the most exalted sublimity of His concealment. And if You witness in Me, O my God, any branch, leaf, or fruit that does not bow down before Him on the day of His appearance, cut it off from that Tree, O God, for it is not of Me and does not return to Me.”

**242** If mention of the Mustaghāth has left you veiled, this call rises from the whole Bayān: “If He were to appear at this very moment, I would be the first to worship Him and the first to bow down before Him.” If you cling to certain words, I have stated with the utmost emphasis that the whole Bayān does not equal a single verse of His.

**243** Now, people, is the one you have chosen instead of Him, whose words you have assumed to be divine verses, more exalted and dearer to you than I and My Bayān? Shame on you for your lack of understanding and your faithlessness! Your greatest delusion and vain imagining is that you have assumed My Revelation to be like the Revelation before it, and you appoint a successor and an executor. You are utterly veiled from the Day of God and its station, and are deprived and unaware of the radiance of the Sun of true unity.

**244** You oppressors! The fragrance of My most pure blood still wafts from My garment. Have the swords of those unbelievers, which they prepared over twelve hundred years with the polish of malice and hatred and tempered with poisons, not sufficed, that you wander once again in the wilderness of these delusions? Be content with what you have done over the course of twelve hundred years. Has it not been revealed in the Bayān: “Do not let names veil you from their Possessor, even the name ‘Prophet,’ for that name is created by His word”?

**245** Glory be to God! Despite the waves of the ocean of the All-Merciful’s utterance, the radiance of the sun of counsel, and the dawning of the luminary of guidance and instruction from the right side of the blessed heart of the Point—may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him—the winds of despair are blowing so fiercely that sorrow has encompassed the world and brought despair to sanctified, illumined hearts. It has seized this transient one in particular so completely that he considers the appearance of anything else impossible.

**246** In the seventh chapter of the second Vāḥid, He says—exalted and mighty are His words: “People of the Bayān! Do not do what the people of the Qurʾān did, thereby rendering the fruits of your own night futile. If, to the extent that you believe in the Bayān, you say at the appearance of His verses, ‘God is our Lord, and we associate no one with Him,’ or ‘This is what God promised us through the Manifestation of Himself; we will invoke nothing alongside Him,’ and if, in whatever state you are, you obey Him, you will have brought forth the fruit of the Bayān. Otherwise, you are unworthy of mention before God. Have mercy on yourselves: if you do not aid the Manifestation of Lordship, do not grieve Him.” And further, He says—exalted is His station: “If you do not attain the presence of God, at least do not grieve the Sign of God. He will forgo any benefit from the followers of the Bayān if you will refrain from harming Him, although I know you will not.” End of quotation.

**247** Glory be to God! Consider how deeply despair had seized that blessed Countenance: despite His countless counsels, firm covenants, binding pledges, and openly declared measures, the greatest despair is evident and manifest in His blessed utterances. Blessed are those who weep.

**248** And from the station of supreme compassion and the realm of awareness, He says—exalted and glorious are His words: “How often He calls a light ‘fire.’” He also says—exalted be His remembrance: “Although I see His appearance as this sun in the midst of heaven, and the setting of all others as the stars of night in the daytime.” Everyone with hearing and sight bears witness that He—may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him—was at all times occupied with mention of the Beloved of all existence, and that through every means of writing, exposition, and admonition He foretold what has proceeded and will proceed from the people of the Bayān.

**249** By the life of my Desire and the Desire of all who are in earth and heaven! His anguish is immense, His sorrow great, and His despair of those in the Bayān greater than any greatness. You heedless ones! Listen to the plea of this transient servant, and do not stain that most pure and holy hem with selfish desires and unworthy fabrications. If you will not turn toward Him, remain silent. He says—exalted be His remembrance: “There is no mention in the Bayān except mention of Him, so that at the time of His appearance He may perhaps experience no sorrow from those who believe in Me.” He has also spoken these blessed words, which are like a light amid the world—exalted and mighty are His words: “The Bayān, from beginning to end, is the repository of all His attributes and the treasury of His fire and His light.”

**250** It is hoped that, through what has been mentioned, the heedless may ascend to the heaven of awareness. As He says—exalted be His remembrance: “If all are educated by the Point of the Bayān and look to the Source, the proof, and the evidence, they will not remain veiled at the time of the appearance.” In this connection He says—exalted are His words: “It is as though one sees all these companions illumined by the honor of faith in that Sun of Truth.” Consider the allusions and explicit statements. He says that it is hoped these companions, meaning the companions then living, will attain the honor of faith, as indeed they did.

**251** The one God is my witness, and the all-knowing True One bears testimony, that this transient one has sincerely set forth, for His sake and for His chosen ones and His loved ones, what will benefit and save the fair-minded. Some of the utterances of the Primal Point—may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him—that were in mind, whether Arabic or Persian, have been cited, although today the Mother of Utterance declares: “The whole Bayān is a mention of Him and is dependent upon and subject to His rejection or acceptance.”

**252** If, through the grace of the True One—exalted be His glory—the horizon of justice and fairness is cleared of the clouds of conjecture and delusion, all will bear witness to what this servant has stated, for everyone knows that no one has been or is as well informed about this matter as this servant. Nevertheless, people who were unaware of the truth have said things that some of the uninformed in the world have taken up, and they have inflicted upon the Ancient Beauty what has made the rock cry out..... End of quotation.

**253** And in the Tablet to Mullā ʿAlī Bajestānī, this has been revealed—exalted are His words:

**254** Whatever has been revealed by the Most Exalted Pen will assuredly come to pass. Read the Sūrih of the Chief, and likewise the Tablet to the King of Paris, which forms part of the blessed Sūrih of the Temple, and also the Tablet of Fuʾād, which was revealed specifically for one of the friends. This Tablet was revealed when the Pasha who was the Ottoman foreign minister had returned to his abode; he had been the cause of the latest upheaval and of the departure from the Land of Mystery to ʿAkkā.

**255** There were two men who, after the Sultan, were the chief authorities: one was Fuʾād Pasha and the other ʿĀlī Pasha. Sometimes the latter was grand vizier and the former chief minister of foreign affairs, and sometimes the reverse. In that Tablet He says—exalted be His majesty: “We will dismiss the one who was like him and seize their ruler who governs the lands, and I am the Almighty, the All-Compelling.”

**256** Likewise, consider in the Book of \[corrupted original text\] the place situated between the two seas. That place means Istanbul, for on one side of it is the White Sea and on the other the Black Sea. In short, everything that has flowed from the Most Exalted Pen has come to pass, and all the other predictions contained in the Tablets will also come to pass. We bear witness that He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Aware....
